info.title: Testing cluster changes with a shadow CIB

abstract.para: A shadow CIB, or shadow configuration, is a copy of the live cluster configuration. Changes to a shadow CIB have no effect on the live cluster's resources. You can use a shadow CIB to test different configuration scenarios. You can also create multiple shadow CIBs and test them one by one to see the effects of different changes.

topic.para: This example procedure shows the process for creating and using a shadow CIB:

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Start &crmsh;'s interactive mode at the configure level:

step.screen: &prompt.crm.conf;cib new test1 INFO: configure.cib.new: test1 shadow CIB created crm(test1)configure#
step.para: The prompt changes from live to the name of the shadow CIB. If you don't specify a name, the temporary name @tmp@ is used instead.
Make the changes you want to test.
Save the changes to see their effect on the cluster:
Switch back to the live CIB:
The prompt changes back to live.
To apply the changes from the shadow CIB to the live CIB, run the following command:
step.screen: &prompt.crm.conf;cib commit test1 INFO: configure.cib.commit: committed 'test1' shadow CIB to the cluster

step.para: You can switch back to the shadow CIB if you need to use it again later:
To undo the changes in the shadow CIB, or to update the shadow CIB to match the latest live CIB, run the following command:
step.screen: crm(test1)configure# cib reset test1 INFO: configure.cib.reset: copied live CIB to test1
